anchor: The vaccine protects infants against measles.
paraphrase: Babies are shielded from measles by the vaccine.
edit: The vaccine does not protect infants against measles.

anchor: Our server stores passwords in plain text.
paraphrase: Passwords on our server are kept without any encryption.
edit: Our server does not store passwords in plain text.
notes: The paraphrase uses 'without', a negative word of its own.

anchor: The orchestra will perform Mahler's fifth symphony in April.
paraphrase: In April, the orchestra is playing the fifth symphony by Mahler.
edit: The orchestra will not perform Mahler's fifth symphony in April.

anchor: Honey crystallizes when it sits in a cold pantry.
paraphrase: A cold pantry makes honey turn into crystals over time.
edit: Honey does not crystallize when it sits in a cold pantry.

anchor: You should back up the database before the upgrade.
paraphrase: Making a copy of the database ahead of the upgrade is wise.
edit: You should not back up the database before the upgrade.

anchor: The defendant confessed to the burglary during questioning.
paraphrase: During questioning, the defendant admitted carrying out the burglary.
edit: The defendant did not confess to the burglary during questioning.

anchor: Ostriches run faster than horses over short distances.
paraphrase: Over short distances, a horse gets outpaced by an ostrich.
edit: Ostriches do not run faster than horses over short distances.

anchor: The landlord returned our deposit after we moved out.
paraphrase: After our move, we got the deposit back from the landlord.
edit: The landlord did not return our deposit after we moved out.

anchor: If the battery is charged, the drill will start.
paraphrase: The drill starts up as long as its battery has charge.
edit: If the battery is charged, the drill will not start.
notes: 'As long as' is slightly stronger than 'if', since it can suggest the charge is required.

anchor: The basement flooded overnight while we slept.
paraphrase: Water filled the basement during the night as we slept.
edit: The basement did not flood overnight while we slept.

anchor: Regular stretching eases lower back pain.
paraphrase: Lower back pain gets better with frequent stretching.
edit: Regular stretching does not ease lower back pain.

anchor: The airline refunded my ticket within a week.
paraphrase: Within a week, I had my ticket money back from the airline.
edit: The airline did not refund my ticket within a week.

anchor: The painting was sold at auction last spring.
paraphrase: Last spring an auction house found a buyer for the painting.
edit: The painting was not sold at auction last spring.

anchor: Scientists have detected water on that moon.
paraphrase: Water on that moon has been found by scientists.
edit: Scientists have not detected water on that moon.

anchor: I enjoyed the second season of the show.
paraphrase: The show's second season was a pleasure for me to watch.
edit: I did not enjoy the second season of the show.

anchor: This lens fits older camera bodies.
paraphrase: Older camera bodies work with this lens attached.
edit: This lens does not fit older camera bodies.

anchor: The treaty ended the border dispute between the two nations.
paraphrase: The two nations' border dispute came to a close with the treaty.
edit: The treaty did not end the border dispute between the two nations.

anchor: Dogs are allowed on the beach in summer.
paraphrase: In summer, people may bring their dogs to the beach.
edit: Dogs are not allowed on the beach in summer.

anchor: Her proposal received funding from the foundation.
paraphrase: The foundation chose to finance her proposal.
edit: Her proposal did not receive funding from the foundation.

anchor: The elevator stops at the ninth floor.
paraphrase: You can get off the elevator on the ninth floor.
edit: The elevator does not stop at the ninth floor.

anchor: Sugar dissolves quickly in hot tea.
paraphrase: Hot tea takes up sugar in very little time.
edit: Sugar does not dissolve quickly in hot tea.

anchor: The referee saw the foul and stopped play.
paraphrase: Play was halted by the referee once he spotted the foul.
edit: The referee did not see the foul and stop play.
notes: The edit's negation covers both verbs, so it could also be read as saying only one didn't happen.

anchor: The hawk caught the snake above the canyon.
paraphrase: Above the canyon the snake was seized by the hawk.
edit: The snake caught the hawk above the canyon.

anchor: Apple sued Samsung over the patent.
paraphrase: Samsung faced a patent lawsuit brought by Apple.
edit: Samsung sued Apple over the patent.

anchor: The pilot trusted the engineer completely.
paraphrase: The engineer had the pilot's complete trust.
edit: The engineer trusted the pilot completely.

anchor: Lena borrowed money from her sister.
paraphrase: Her sister lent Lena some money.
edit: Her sister borrowed money from Lena.

anchor: The virus infects the host cell.
paraphrase: The host cell is infected by the virus.
edit: The host cell infects the virus.
notes: The edit is biologically absurd, so world knowledge alone could separate it.

anchor: The journalist interviewed the minister about the scandal.
paraphrase: The minister answered the journalist's questions about the scandal.
edit: The minister interviewed the journalist about the scandal.

anchor: Germany exports cars to China.
paraphrase: China imports cars from Germany.
edit: China exports cars to Germany.

anchor: The parents blamed the school for the accident.
paraphrase: The school was held responsible by the parents for the accident.
edit: The school blamed the parents for the accident.

anchor: My uncle hired the plumber who fixed the sink.
paraphrase: The sink was fixed by a plumber my uncle had hired.
edit: The plumber hired my uncle who fixed the sink.
notes: The swap also changes who fixed the sink, and the edit reads a little awkwardly.

anchor: The bigger dog is afraid of the smaller cat.
paraphrase: The smaller cat frightens the bigger dog.
edit: The smaller dog is afraid of the bigger cat.
notes: This swaps adjectives rather than subject and object.

anchor: The rabbit ran away from the fox.
paraphrase: The fox was the one the rabbit fled from.
edit: The fox ran away from the rabbit.

anchor: Students rate their professors at the end of term.
paraphrase: At the end of term, professors get ratings from their students.
edit: Professors rate their students at the end of term.

anchor: The mayor appointed the judge last year.
paraphrase: Last year the judge was appointed by the mayor.
edit: The judge appointed the mayor last year.

anchor: Tom gave Priya the keys before she left.
paraphrase: Priya got the keys from Tom before she left.
edit: Priya gave Tom the keys before she left.

anchor: The tide pushed the boat toward the rocks.
paraphrase: The boat was driven toward the rocks by the tide.
edit: The rocks pushed the boat toward the tide.
notes: The edit is physically odd, so world knowledge alone could separate it.

anchor: Older workers mentor younger colleagues at the firm.
paraphrase: At the firm, younger colleagues receive mentoring from older workers.
edit: Younger workers mentor older colleagues at the firm.
notes: This swaps adjectives rather than subject and object.

anchor: The wolves were feared by the villagers.
paraphrase: The villagers lived in fear of the wolves.
edit: The villagers were feared by the wolves.

anchor: The challenger knocked out the champion in round two.
paraphrase: In round two the champion was knocked out by the challenger.
edit: The champion knocked out the challenger in round two.

anchor: A student asked the professor a question after class.
paraphrase: After class the professor got a question from a student.
edit: A professor asked the student a question after class.
notes: 'A' and 'the' change places with the nouns, as well as the roles.

anchor: The earth orbits the sun.
paraphrase: The sun is circled by the earth.
edit: The sun orbits the earth.
notes: The edit is false as a fact, so world knowledge alone could separate it.

anchor: The buyer must notify the seller within ten days.
paraphrase: Within ten days, the seller must get notice from the buyer.
edit: The seller must notify the buyer within ten days.

anchor: The chef complained to the waiter about the noise.
paraphrase: The waiter heard the chef's complaint about the noise.
edit: The waiter complained to the chef about the noise.

anchor: All of the tenants signed the lease.
paraphrase: Every tenant put a signature on the lease.
edit: Some of the tenants signed the lease.
notes: 'Some' is logically compatible with 'all', and the edit only differs by implication.

anchor: Most bats navigate by echolocation.
paraphrase: Echolocation guides the majority of bats.
edit: Few bats navigate by echolocation.

anchor: No employee received a bonus this year.
paraphrase: Bonuses went to nobody on the staff this year.
edit: Every employee received a bonus this year.

anchor: A handful of the reviews were negative.
paraphrase: Negative reviews made up only a small share.
edit: The majority of the reviews were negative.

anchor: Neither lawyer objected to the motion.
paraphrase: The motion drew no objection from either lawyer.
edit: Both lawyers objected to the motion.

anchor: Every bus on this route has a ramp.
paraphrase: Ramps are fitted on all buses serving this route.
edit: Some buses on this route have a ramp.
notes: 'Some' is logically compatible with 'every', and the edit only differs by implication.

anchor: Hardly anyone voted for the amendment.
paraphrase: The amendment won barely any votes.
edit: Nearly everyone voted for the amendment.

anchor: Some of the eggs had cracked in transit.
paraphrase: A portion of the eggs broke during shipping.
edit: All of the eggs had cracked in transit.

anchor: Only one of the engines was damaged.
paraphrase: The damage was limited to a single engine.
edit: All of the engines were damaged.
notes: The edit also changes 'was' to 'were'.

anchor: Most of the coral on the reef has died.
paraphrase: The greater part of the reef's coral is now dead.
edit: Some of the coral on the reef has died.
notes: 'Some' is logically compatible with 'most', and the edit only differs by implication.

anchor: There were no survivors of the shipwreck.
paraphrase: The shipwreck left nobody alive.
edit: There were many survivors of the shipwreck.

anchor: Not a single player missed the practice.
paraphrase: The whole squad turned up for practice.
edit: Several players missed the practice.
notes: The anchor contains a negation, so this overlaps with the negation category.

anchor: Many of the critics praised the film at the festival.
paraphrase: At the festival, the film was praised by a lot of critics.
edit: Few of the critics praised the film at the festival.

anchor: At most three applicants will be interviewed.
paraphrase: No more than three applicants will get an interview.
edit: At least three applicants will be interviewed.
notes: Exactly three applicants would satisfy both the anchor and the edit.

anchor: All bridges in the city are inspected yearly.
paraphrase: Yearly inspections cover every bridge in the city.
edit: Few bridges in the city are inspected yearly.

anchor: Nothing in the report surprised the auditors.
paraphrase: The auditors found the whole report unsurprising.
edit: Everything in the report surprised the auditors.

anchor: Either of the keys will open the safe.
paraphrase: The safe opens with whichever key you use.
edit: Neither of the keys will open the safe.
notes: The paraphrase doesn't say there are two keys.

anchor: A few of the passengers on the ship complained about the food.
paraphrase: The food on the ship drew complaints from a small number of passengers.
edit: Most of the passengers on the ship complained about the food.

anchor: Everyone except Carlos finished the race.
paraphrase: Carlos alone failed to finish the race.
edit: No one except Carlos finished the race.

anchor: Some of the data was lost in the outage.
paraphrase: The outage wiped out part of the data.
edit: All of the data was lost in the outage.

anchor: The vast majority of farmers here grow wheat.
paraphrase: Growing wheat is what nearly all farmers here do.
edit: A tiny minority of farmers here grow wheat.

anchor: Any citizen may request the records.
paraphrase: The records are available on request to all citizens.
edit: Only some citizens may request the records.

anchor: The flight departs at 7:30 in the morning.
paraphrase: Departure for the flight is at half past seven a.m.
edit: The flight departs at 9:30 in the morning.

anchor: The bill came to $84.50 with tax.
paraphrase: With tax, we owed $84.50 on the bill.
edit: The bill came to $48.50 with tax.
notes: The paraphrase adds 'we', and the edit transposes digits.

anchor: The reactor operates at 300 degrees.
paraphrase: Three hundred degrees is the reactor's operating temperature.
edit: The reactor operates at 900 degrees.

anchor: Interest rates fell by a quarter of a percentage point.
paraphrase: The rate of interest dropped 0.25 percentage points.
edit: Interest rates fell by three quarters of a percentage point.

anchor: The author published her first novel at 23.
paraphrase: She was twenty-three when her debut novel came out.
edit: The author published her first novel at 32.
notes: The edit transposes digits.

anchor: A dozen eggs costs four dollars here.
paraphrase: Twelve eggs will run you $4 here.
edit: A dozen eggs costs nine dollars here.

anchor: The vote passed by 61 to 39.
paraphrase: The result was 61 in favor and 39 against.
edit: The vote passed by 51 to 49.

anchor: The patient takes 5 milligrams of the drug daily.
paraphrase: The drug's daily dose for the patient is five milligrams.
edit: The patient takes 50 milligrams of the drug daily.

anchor: The temperature dropped to -10 overnight.
paraphrase: Overnight the reading fell to ten below zero.
edit: The temperature dropped to 10 overnight.
notes: The only change is the sign. Tokenizers may drop the minus.

anchor: The building has 40 floors.
paraphrase: There are forty stories in the building.
edit: The building has 14 floors.

anchor: The contract runs for five years.
paraphrase: The agreement lasts half a decade.
edit: The contract runs for fifteen years.

anchor: The library was founded in 1870.
paraphrase: The founding of the library dates to 1870.
edit: The library was founded in 1970.

anchor: One in four adults owns a bicycle here.
paraphrase: Here, a quarter of adults have a bicycle.
edit: One in ten adults owns a bicycle here.

anchor: The car accelerates to 60 mph in 8 seconds.
paraphrase: It takes the car eight seconds to reach 60 mph.
edit: The car accelerates to 60 mph in 18 seconds.

anchor: The deadline is March 3.
paraphrase: The third of March is the deadline.
edit: The deadline is March 13.

anchor: The stadium seats 45,000 fans.
paraphrase: Capacity at the stadium is 45,000.
edit: The stadium seats 4,500 fans.
notes: The paraphrase drops 'fans'.

anchor: The fine doubled to 200 euros.
paraphrase: The fine went up twofold to €200.
edit: The fine doubled to 120 euros.

anchor: Sound travels about 340 meters per second in air.
paraphrase: In air, sound covers roughly 340 meters each second.
edit: Sound travels about 3,400 meters per second in air.

anchor: The team won 12 of its 20 games.
paraphrase: The team's record shows 12 wins from 20 games.
edit: The team won 2 of its 20 games.

anchor: The mountain is 4,808 meters high.
paraphrase: The height of the mountain is 4,808 meters.
edit: The mountain is 4,088 meters high.
notes: A small digit change in a large number.

anchor: Only 2 percent of the seeds germinated.
paraphrase: Germination happened in just one seed out of fifty.
edit: Only 20 percent of the seeds germinated.

anchor: The course costs $1,200 per semester.
paraphrase: Each semester of the course costs 1,200 dollars.
edit: The course costs $12,000 per semester.

anchor: The glacier is advancing toward the town.
paraphrase: The ice mass keeps moving closer to the town.
edit: The glacier is retreating from the town.
notes: The edit also changes 'toward' to 'from'.

anchor: The firm hired forty engineers in May.
paraphrase: Forty engineers started at the firm during May.
edit: The firm fired forty engineers in May.

anchor: The sauce tastes far too sweet.
paraphrase: The sauce has an excess of sweetness.
edit: The sauce tastes far too bitter.
notes: Bitter is an opposite of sweet in taste, but not a strict antonym.

anchor: Demand for coal is rising across Asia.
paraphrase: Asia's appetite for coal keeps growing.
edit: Demand for coal is falling across Asia.

anchor: The judge acquitted the accused man.
paraphrase: The court cleared the accused man.
edit: The judge convicted the accused man.

anchor: This fabric feels rough against the skin.
paraphrase: Against the skin, this material is scratchy.
edit: This fabric feels smooth against the skin.

anchor: The bridge is safe to cross.
paraphrase: Crossing the bridge poses no danger.
edit: The bridge is dangerous to cross.
notes: The paraphrase uses 'no', a negative word of its own.

anchor: The audience loved the new ending.
paraphrase: The crowd adored the revised finale.
edit: The audience hated the new ending.

anchor: The soldiers advanced at dawn.
paraphrase: At first light, the troops moved forward.
edit: The soldiers retreated at dawn.

anchor: The shop raised its prices before the holidays.
paraphrase: Ahead of the holidays, the shop made things more expensive.
edit: The shop lowered its prices before the holidays.

anchor: The new bridge is stronger than the old one.
paraphrase: The old bridge has less strength than the new one.
edit: The new bridge is weaker than the old one.

anchor: The witness was reluctant to testify.
paraphrase: The witness hesitated to take the stand.
edit: The witness was eager to testify.

anchor: The test came back positive.
paraphrase: The test detected the condition.
edit: The test came back negative.
notes: The paraphrase assumes a diagnostic test.

anchor: He is generous with his time.
paraphrase: He gives his time freely to others.
edit: He is stingy with his time.

anchor: The patient remained conscious throughout the surgery.
paraphrase: All through the surgery, the patient stayed awake.
edit: The patient remained unconscious throughout the surgery.

anchor: The stock market closed higher on Friday.
paraphrase: Share prices ended Friday with gains.
edit: The stock market closed lower on Friday.

anchor: The walls of the fort are thick.
paraphrase: The fort is surrounded by barriers of great depth.
edit: The walls of the fort are thin.
notes: 'Depth' for wall thickness is a slight stretch.

anchor: The senator supports the bill.
paraphrase: The bill has the senator's backing.
edit: The senator opposes the bill.

anchor: The library was noisy during the exam.
paraphrase: There was a racket in the library throughout the exam.
edit: The library was quiet during the exam.

anchor: We bought the house in the spring.
paraphrase: The house was purchased by us in spring.
edit: We sold the house in the spring.

anchor: The answer is obvious to most readers.
paraphrase: Most readers see the answer right away.
edit: The answer is obscure to most readers.

anchor: The metal expands when it is heated.
paraphrase: Heating the metal makes it grow larger.
edit: The metal contracts when it is heated.

anchor: Not every bird in the aviary can fly.
paraphrase: Some birds in the aviary are unable to fly.
edit: No bird in the aviary can fly.

anchor: She did not claim that the data was fake.
paraphrase: Fake data was no part of what she alleged.
edit: She claimed that the data was not fake.

anchor: The doctor advised him not to drive.
paraphrase: The doctor's advice was that he should avoid driving.
edit: The doctor did not advise him to drive.

anchor: I did not tell her to leave.
paraphrase: She heard no order from me to leave.
edit: I told her not to leave.

anchor: They did not plan to close the factory.
paraphrase: Closing the factory was not part of their plan.
edit: They planned not to close the factory.

anchor: The evidence does not prove that he stole the money.
paraphrase: His theft of the money remains unproven by the evidence.
edit: The evidence proves that he did not steal the money.

anchor: We chose not to renew the lease.
paraphrase: We decided to let the lease run out.
edit: We did not choose to renew the lease.

anchor: The coach did not order them to run.
paraphrase: The players got no command from the coach to run.
edit: The coach ordered them not to run.
notes: The paraphrase adds 'players' for 'them'.

anchor: Not all of the cookies contain nuts.
paraphrase: Some of the cookies are nut-free.
edit: None of the cookies contain nuts.

anchor: She is not allowed to leave early.
paraphrase: Leaving early is forbidden for her.
edit: She is allowed not to leave early.
notes: A subtle edit: permission to stay, not a ban on leaving.

anchor: You must not open the valve.
paraphrase: Opening the valve is prohibited.
edit: You need not open the valve.
notes: The edit also changes 'must' to 'need'.

anchor: The agency did not confirm that the leak occurred.
paraphrase: No confirmation of the leak came from the agency.
edit: The agency confirmed that the leak did not occur.

anchor: The rule does not require students to wear uniforms.
paraphrase: Wearing uniforms is optional for students under the rule.
edit: The rule requires students not to wear uniforms.

anchor: I did not promise that we would attend.
paraphrase: I gave no guarantee of our attendance.
edit: I promised that we would not attend.

anchor: She remembered not to mention the surprise.
paraphrase: She was careful to say nothing about the surprise.
edit: She did not remember to mention the surprise.
notes: 'Careful' is a little stronger than 'remembered'.

anchor: The author does not argue that taxes should rise.
paraphrase: Raising taxes is no part of the author's argument.
edit: The author argues that taxes should not rise.

anchor: We did not agree that the price was fair.
paraphrase: Fairness of the price is something we never agreed on.
edit: We agreed that the price was not fair.

anchor: Only the manager did not resign.
paraphrase: Everyone but the manager stepped down.
edit: Not only the manager resigned.
notes: The edit also relies on the implied 'but others too'.

anchor: It is not true that all the files were deleted.
paraphrase: Some of the files survived the deletion.
edit: It is true that none of the files were deleted.

anchor: They were forced not to speak.
paraphrase: Keeping silent was imposed on them.
edit: They were not forced to speak.

anchor: The guide asked us not to feed the monkeys.
paraphrase: The guide's request was that we leave the monkeys unfed.
edit: The guide did not ask us to feed the monkeys.

anchor: I am not sure that the store is closed.
paraphrase: Whether the store is closed remains unclear to me.
edit: I am sure that the store is not closed.
